items.back: Every row is created as `{ ...item, userId }` (`settings/import/route.ts` lines 26-71) with no schema. Because `userId` is spread last, the caller cannot forge it, but they choose `id`, `projectId`, `areaId`, `taskId`, `goalId` and every other column. An `id` that already belongs to another user's row makes `createMany` violate the primary key, and the route has no `try/catch`, so the request errors instead of returning `{ ok: true }` — another existence oracle. Fix: validate each collection with a Zod schema, regenerate ids, and remap foreign keys through an old-id → new-id table built from the caller's own imported rows.

items.label: f01-two-predicates
items.front: Reviewer says 'PATCH already filters by userId, so the project check is redundant' (src/app/api/tasks/[id]/route.ts:23-36). Give the counterexample.
items.back: Alice owns task A; Bob owns project B. Alice PATCHes A with projectId B. updateMany({ where: { id: A, userId: Alice } }) matches, so without the guard A points into Bob's project. The project query needs { id: B, userId: Alice }, the task write needs { id: A, userId: Alice }: neither predicate replaces the other.

`handleError` returns `error.message` with 400 for any `Error` (`src/lib/api.ts` lines 24-25). `POST /api/projects` with a nonexistent `areaId` fails the `Project_areaId_fkey` constraint and returns the Prisma message; with Bob's real `areaId` it returns 201. The difference tells a caller whether an id exists, and the raw message exposes internals. The fix is an ownership lookup that returns the same 404 for both, plus a generic message for non-validation errors.

items.label: f03-ownership-guard-shape
items.front: Write the shape of the destination ownership guard used in POST /api/tasks (src/app/api/tasks/route.ts:38-44).
items.back: findFirst({ where: { id: body.projectId, userId: auth.user.id }, select: { id: true } }); if nothing comes back, return 404 'Project not found' before any write. One predicate pair proves the relationship is allowed at that moment.

items.label: f04-handleerror
items.front: What does handleError (src/lib/api.ts:13-29) return for a ZodError, for any other Error, and for a non-Error throw?
items.back: ZodError: 400 'Validation failed' with the issues. Any other Error: 400 with error.message verbatim - which is how raw Prisma constraint messages leak to clients. Anything else: 500 'Unknown error'.

items.front: 2: The write becomes a read leak.
items.back: `GET /api/day` includes `dayTask.task.project.area` (`day/route.ts` lines 27-37) and `GET /api/widgets` includes `goal` (line 13). Once Alice's DayTask points at Bob's task, Alice's day view returns Bob's task title, project name and area name. Precondition: Alice must already know Bob's id. Ids are `cuid()` (`schema.prisma`), so this is not enumerable, but the invariant is broken.

items.label: f02-sibling-routes
items.front: The worked change fixed tasks only. Name the bug class still open in POST /api/daytask (src/app/api/daytask/route.ts:33-42) and its siblings.
items.back: Unchecked relationship ids: body.taskId (and goalId, areaId elsewhere) is written without looking the target up with the caller's userId. Once a DayTask points at Bob's task, GET /api/day's includes turn the write into a read leak of Bob's task, project and area names.
